messages:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: EU1 GPU pool saturation detected. 95th perc latency > 2x SLO, queue depth rising. autoscaler error: hit scale_limit.
inc-bot: Affected routes: /v1/generate (primary eu1). Estimated queued requests: 14.2k. Customer impact: degraded perf for customers on eu region.
kai (oncall): acked. I'm on it, jumping in to triage.
leila (sre): I'm pulling metrics. Looks like sustained enqueue rate spike after 10:05 UTC, autoscaler tried to provision but failed with quota error from cloud provider: "GPU quota exceeded".
tom (infra): Confirmed. Quota requests pending approval; we didn't hit them yet but the infra autoscaler bumped to limit=64 and provider returned 403.
maya (runtime): Runtime logs show many pending KV cache warmups and memory fragmentation. Evictions kicked in, which increased token latency. Sample log:
```
[10:12:41] runtime: request enqueue id=abc123 seq=1 tokens=512
[10:12:42] runtime: eviction triggered pool=primary-eu1 reason=mem_pressure
[10:12:45] autoscaler: scale_attempt -> desired=80, provision_error=QuotaExceeded
[10:12:50] router: spillover -> route=eu2 (probabilistic 5%)
```

kai (oncall): So autoscaler couldn't add nodes; routing started to probabilistically spill to eu2 but most traffic still pins to eu1. We need a coordinated spillover to us-west and a temporary throttle policy for heavy routes.
leila (sre): Agree. Plan: 1) apply temporary concurrency quota on /v1/generate to slow enqueue 2) increase spillover weight to eu2/us-west immediately 3) manually evict low-priority jobs from eu1 queue 4) notify customers on impacted SLAs.
natalie (support): I'll draft a status note. Which customers are highest priority? We have two enterprise tenants on direct reserved capacity in eu1.
maya (runtime): Those two tenants are pinned to dedicated pools; we need a manual handshake to evict only non-pinned jobs. I'll run a filter.
tom (infra): I can push a route update. Command I'm about to run (doing it in 30s):
```
# increase spillover to us-west & eu2
cli redwood route update --region eu1 --spillover "us-west=0.35,eu2=0.35,local=0.3"
```
kai (oncall): Hold on route change until we set throttles, otherwise queuing will shift without reducing load. Leila, can you apply the concurrency limit?
leila (sre): Applying concurrency limit of 8 per-client on /v1/generate now.
leila (sre): `policy apply --route /v1/generate --concurrency 8 --scope client` -> applied.
ops-bot: :white_check_mark: policy applied: /v1/generate concurrency 8 (scope: client).
leila (sre): Now increasing spillover weights. Doing the route update.
ops-bot: :rotating_light: route update in progress...
tom (infra): Route update complete. New weights: us-west 0.35, eu2 0.35, eu1 0.3.
maya (runtime): Observing immediate drop in eu1 enqueue rate by ~42%, latencies starting to normalize on a per-request basis. Queue still has ~9k backlogged; we'll need to drain that.
kai (oncall): Start eviction of non-pinned workloads in eu1. Maya, run the eviction script with exclude for tenants A and B.
maya (runtime): Running:
```
python tools/evict_queue.py --pool eu1 --exclude-tenants tenantA,tenantB --batch-size 120
```
maya (runtime): Eviction running. First batch removed ~1100 tasks, CPU and GPU utilization dropped 8%.
leila (sre): Support: Natalie, customer-facing note: we have applied throttles and spillover, some customers in eu1 may see increased latency; dedicated tenants should be unaffected. Recommend internal classification: "degraded".
natalie (support): Draft ready, posting to status page and pinging the two affected enterprise contacts with targeted message.
ops-bot: :chart_with_upwards_trend: metrics: eu1 queue depth: 14.2k -> 9.1k -> 6.3k over 18 minutes. 95th latency: 2.5s -> 1.3s.
kai (oncall): Good. Next: open a quota ticket with cloud provider to raise GPU quota in eu1 (sourced to infra). Tom, you take that?
tom (infra): On it. Ticket created: CLOUD-8921. ETA for review ~2 hours. I'll request expedited review.
leila (sre): Also flagging autoscaler fallback: we should have a longer tail plan for quota failure: a soft queue shed or transparent fallback to smaller quantized model variant (e.g., gpt-small) for excess requests. Maya, can runtime expose that?
maya (runtime): Yes, we have model-variant fallback ready, need a route-level policy toggle. I'll prepare a canary policy to redirect 20% of overflow to quantized model.
leila (sre): Create the canary now but keep low to avoid quality regressions.
maya (runtime): Canary applied: overflow->gpt-q20 (20%). Observing reduced pressure on memory and faster completion for canary stream.
ops-bot: :white_check_mark: canary policy active.
kai (oncall): Looks stable. Queue draining steadily. Handing off to night oncall in 2h. I'll remain reachable for escalations.
leila (sre): Post-incident follow-ups: (1) autobump flow: add better quota-detection in autoscaler to proactively switch routing before hitting provider quota (2) runbook update: add eviction handshake steps and support notification template (3) telemetry: add token-level cost heatmaps to identify sudden bursts.
tom (infra): I'll add expedited quota workflow and attempt to pre-warm additional nodes when traffic ramps.
maya (runtime): We'll add the small-model fallback as a first-class policy for heavy routes.
natalie (support): Status page updated, customers notified. No customers have reported SLA breaches yet; monitoring for complaints.
kai (oncall): Final note: incident classified as Severity 2 (degraded service); root cause: sudden traffic spike + provider GPU quota limit; mitigations: concurrency throttles, spillover weight change, manual eviction, canary quantized fallback. I'll create the incident ticket with timeline and assign follow-ups.
leila (sre): Thanks team. Handoff to @eve (night-oncall) in 2 hours. Kai, please ping if rollback needed.
ops-bot: :pager: handoff scheduled to eve in 120 minutes.
inc-bot: Incident thread closed pending follow-up actions.
